newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet puts off decision on feed tariff cuts.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet puts off decision on feed tariff cuts.

text.p: The government dropped from Tuesday's cabinet meeting agenda a commerce ministry proposal to reduce tariffs on imported feeds, a government official said.
The official said the issue was not among the items discussed by the cabinet.

Industry sources said the plan could be delayed for some time as the meeting was likely to be the last for Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's administration following the premier's announcement on Saturday that he would resign within seven days.

The commerce ministry had proposed reducing import duties to 10 percent from 15 percent for soymeal, to zero from five percent for soybeans, to zero from three percent for corn and to 15 percent plus a 140 baht/tonne surcharge from six percent plus 1,400 baht on fishmeal.
The aim was to help reduce production costs for the meat and poultry industries.
